item.title: Air Canada attendants strike: Carrier cancels flights ahead of work stoppage — Here’s what passengers can do
item.description: Air Canada initiated flight cancellations on Thursday following a 72-hour strike notice from flight attendants, potentially disrupting travel for hundreds of thousands. The airline anticipates a complete operational shutdown by early Saturday, affecting approximately 130,000 people daily and stranding 25,000 Canadians abroad. Air Canada will provide full refunds and alternative travel arrangements where feasible.

item.title: ‘Putin won’t mess around with me’: Trump ahead of meeting in Alaska; US president says Russia, Ukraine ‘will make peace’
item.description: President Trump asserted that Vladimir Putin won't "mess around" with him ahead of their summit in Alaska, where they plan to discuss a potential ceasefire in Ukraine. Trump believes Putin desires full control of Ukraine but insists this won't happen under his presidency. He also proposed a second meeting involving European leaders and Volodymyr Zelenskyy to foster peace negotiations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Chicago shooting: Man killed while livestreaming on Facebook; second murder on Austin block this week
item.description: In a shocking incident in Chicago's South Austin, 42-year-old Kevin Watson was fatally shot while livestreaming on Facebook. The incident occurred on the 5000 block of West Madison Street. Gunfire erupted moments after Watson exited a car, with the assailant firing from another vehicle.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'We have Tony Soparno': George Conway compares Trump to fictional character; remarks made over federal takeover of DC
item.description: George Conway, a critic of Donald Trump, likened him to Tony Soprano. This happened after Trump's federal control of Washington DC. Conway and Miles Taylor discussed Trump's actions on MSNBC. Trump cited 'out of control' crime as the reason. Conway criticized Trump's intimidation tactics. Taylor described facing repercussions for criticizing Trump.

item.title: ‘Take a drug test’: Donald Trump targets Elizabeth Warren; sparks Social Security debate at White House
item.description: Donald Trump suggested Elizabeth Warren undergo a drug test. This came after Warren's claims about Trump's Social Security cuts. Trump defended his administration's Social Security approach. He criticized Warren's past claims and her support for a New York mayoral candidate. Warren had accused the Trump administration of weakening Social Security. She proposed measures to strengthen the system and expand benefits.

item.title: ChatGPT health scare: 60-year-old man hospitalized after following AI advice- Here's why
item.description: A 60-year-old man landed in hospital after following ChatGPT's advice. He replaced table salt with sodium bromide. The man showed paranoia and hallucinations. Doctors found high bromide levels in his body. He was trying to eliminate table salt from his diet. ChatGPT suggested bromide as a chloride replacement. The AI chatbot did not provide health warnings.

item.title: Free speech clash: Supreme Court allows Mississippi's law requiring age verification for minors; tech giants oppose mandate
item.description: The US Supreme Court has allowed Mississippi's law requiring age verification and parental consent for minors on social media to remain in effect while legal challenges proceed. NetChoice, representing major social media platforms, sought to block the law, arguing it violates the First Amendment.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Six or seven planes came down': Trump again claims he solved India-Pakistan issue; 'they were ready to go'
item.description: Donald Trump claimed to have brokered peace between India and Pakistan ahead of his Alaska summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin. "Six or seven planes came down. They were ready to go. Maybe nuclear. We solved that," Trump said about the India-Pakistan tension. Air Chief Marshal Staff Amar Preet Singh recently said India shot down five Pakistani fighter jets and one other large aircraft during Operation Sindoor. Pakistan rejected the claim.

item.title: Olympic Gold Medalist Chloe Kim shows up at boyfriend Myles Garrett’s Browns practice
item.description: Despite a recent speeding incident where Myles Garrett was fined, his girlfriend, Chloe Kim, showed unwavering support by attending his practice. The couple's affection was evident as they were visibly captivated by each other during interviews and red-carpet photos. Their relationship, which began three months ago, continues to flourish amidst Garrett's NFL preseason preparations.

item.title: Sandwich assault arrest: DOJ worker fired after allegedly attacking CBP agent in DC; incident caught on video
item.description: A Department of Justice employee, Sean Charles Dunn, was fired after allegedly assaulting a Customs and Border Protection agent with a Subway sandwich in Washington D.C. The incident occurred on Sunday night, where Dunn reportedly shouted at federal officers, calling them "fascists," before throwing the sandwich.

item.title: ‘100% I’ll get him out’: Trump vows to free jailed Hong Kong tycoon Jimmy Lai; Beijing warns against foreign interference
item.description: Donald Trump pledged to secure the release of Jimmy Lai, the jailed Hong Kong media tycoon, vowing to raise the issue with Xi Jinping during trade negotiations. Lai, a critic of China's Communist Party, faces charges under the national security law. His case has drawn international attention, with supporters expressing concern for his health and advocating for his freedom.

item.title: Surging crime: New Mexico’s governor declares emergency; comes days after Trump took control of DC police
item.description: Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham declared a state of emergency in Rio Arriba County, New Mexico, due to escalating violence and drug trafficking, particularly driven by fentanyl. The declaration allocates $750,000 to bolster local law enforcement and emergency management. This action follows rising concerns from local and tribal leaders about the overwhelming impact on communities and resources.

item.title: Russia-US talks: Were tariffs on India a way to get Putin to come to the table? What Trump said
item.description: Donald Trump suggested that secondary tariffs on India, impacting Russian oil sales, might have influenced Vladimir Putin's decision to meet him in Alaska. Trump aims for a quick peace deal in Ukraine, potentially involving Volodymyr Zelenskyy in future talks. Increased tariffs on Indian imports have drawn strong objections, highlighting the complex global dynamics surrounding the US-Russia relationship.

item.title: Epstein connection controversy: Hunter Biden dismisses Melania Trump’s defamation threat; claims, 'That's not going to happen'
item.description: Hunter Biden has dismissed Melania Trump's threat to sue him for $1 billion over his claims linking her to Jeffrey Epstein. Biden asserted that Epstein introduced Melania to Donald Trump, a claim the Trumps deny. Melania's legal team demanded a retraction, citing reputational harm.

item.title: Mega-tsunami warning: Could a 1,000-foot tsunami hit the US Pacific Coast? Scientist raises alarm
item.description: A Virginia Tech study warns of a potential mega-tsunami along the US Pacific Coast, triggered by a major earthquake in the Cascadia Subduction Zone. Coastal regions face sudden land subsidence and massive waves, posing unprecedented risks to millions. Researchers urge immediate action for improved early-warning systems and resilient infrastructure to minimize potential devastation.
